en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 13.11.
Sekkhattika (The Triplet on the Trainee)
Dependent on a state that is subject to training (*sekkha*), a state that is not subject to training (*naasekkha*) arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is subject to training, a state that is not subject to training arises by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state that is subject to training, a state that is neither subject to training nor not subject to training...
A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state of one in training (sekha), states that are neither-of-training-nor-beyond-training arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state of one in training, states that are beyond-training and neither-of-training-nor-beyond-training arise by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state appertaining to one beyond training (asekkha), a state not appertaining to one beyond training arises by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya). Dependent on a state appertaining to one beyond training, a state appertaining to one who is in training (sekkha) arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state appertaining to one beyond training, a state that is neither-appertaining-to-one-beyond-training-nor-appertaining-to-one-in-training arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state appertaining to one beyond training, a state appertaining to one who is in training and a state that is neither-appertaining-to-one-beyond-training-nor-appertaining-to-one-in-training [arise]...

And states arise conditioned by the root-cause. Dependent on a state of one beyond training (asekkha), states that are neither of one beyond training nor of one in training (naasekkha) arise conditioned by the root-cause.

Dependent on a state that is neither of one beyond training nor of one in training (nevasekkhanāsekkha), a state of one beyond training arises conditioned by the root-cause. [Dependent on] a state that is neither of one beyond training nor of one in training...
Dependent on a state that is neither-learner-nor-non-learner (n’asekkha), a state that is not-a-learner (nāsekkha) arises by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya).

Dependent on a state that is neither-learner-nor-non-learner, states that are both not-a-learner and neither-learner-nor-non-learner arise by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is both a-learner (sekkha) and neither-learner-nor-non-learner, a state that is not-a-learner arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is both in training (*sekkha*) and neither-in-training-nor-beyond-training (*nevasekkhanāsekkha*), a state that is beyond training (*naasekkha*) arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is both in training and neither-in-training-nor-beyond-training, states that are both beyond training and neither-in-training-nor-beyond-training arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is both beyond training and neither-in-training-nor-beyond-training, a state that is beyond training arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a state that is both beyond training (*asekkha*) and neither-in-training-nor-beyond-training (*nevasekkhanāsekkha*), a state that is not beyond training arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is both beyond training and neither-in-training-nor-beyond-training, states that are both not beyond training and not beyond training arise by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are nineteen; in the case of the object condition, nine ... [and so on] ... in the case of the non-disappearance condition, nineteen. (The full detail applies in all cases.)
